title: Instructions for the cipher with Baron Stosch and Mr Walton, TNA SP 106/7 (DECODE R597)

steps.what: Fetched DECODE metadata for R597 and R598 and the two R597 images with the stored cookie.
Recognised the record as an English instruction sheet with a worked French example, not a ciphered letter; transcribed it, including the interlinear syllables over every group.
Identified DECODE's 'unsolved lines' as the same Key B example written run-on without separators.
Dated the sheet c. 1731 from Stosch (alias John Walton) and the correction Rome -> Florence.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): R597 linked to transcription.txt, which holds the groups with the writer's own interlinear syllables (transcription and reading in one file)

texts.label: R597, SP 106/7 f. 33, instruction sheet (c. 1731)
texts.summary: Not a ciphered letter but an English instruction sheet sent with a cipher 'which serves only to correspond with Baron Stosch and Mr Walton' (Philipp von Stosch, the British spy on the Stuart court, who signed as John Walton), c. 1731. It explains a three-figure syllabic code with two keys, A and B, used alternately, with the worked example 'Les Adherens du Pretendant se donnent beaucoup de mouvement à Rome'; every group has its syllable written above it, so the one file is both transcription and reading.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (plain bar, VERIFY5_BRIEF): English of c. 1731: plain bar. transcription.txt is a clear instruction sheet with digit tables; its prose (tables and syllable rows cut): plain 0.706 (12/17), explicit holes 0.882; the failures are the French example sentence and the digit run. Keeps read.

prior.where: DECODE record note describes the sheet (letter-pair nomenclator) but calls lines unsolved; the interlinear syllables are the writer's own.
